source_text: Ὅλως δὲ κἂν συγχωρήσῃ τις τὴν ἐκ τούτων εἰσιοῦσαν τροφήν (προσειρήσθω δὲ τοῦτο συνηθέστερον), καίπερ οὖσαν παρὰ φύσιν, διακρίνεσθαι καὶ ματαβάλλειν εἰς ἕν τι τῶν ὑγραινόντων ἢ ξηραινόντων ἢ θερμαινόντων ἢ ψυχόντων, οὐδ᾿ οὕτως ἐκ τῶν συγχωρηθέντων αὐτοῖς γενήσεταί τι προὔργου, τῶν μὲν ἀνισταμένων σωμάτων ἐκ τῶν οἰκείων μερῶν πάλιν συνισταμένων, οὐδενὸς δὲ τῶν εἰρημένων μέρους ὄντος, οὐδὲ τὴν ὡς μέρους ἐπέχοντος σχέσιν ἢ τάξιν, οὐ μὴν οὐδὲ παραμένοντος πάντοτε τοῖς τρεφομένοις τοῦ σώματος μέρεσιν, ἢ συνανισταμένου τοῖς ἀνισταμένοις, οὐδὲν συντελοῦντος ἔτι πρὸς τὸ ζῆν οὐχ αἵματος οὐ φλέγματος οὐ χολῆς οὐ πνεύματος. Οὐδὲ γὰρ ὦν ἐδεήθη ποτὲ τὰ τρεφόμενα σώματα δεηθήσεται καὶ τότε, συνανῃρημένης τῇ τῶν τρεφομένων ἐνδείᾳ καὶ φθορᾷ τῆς ἐξ ὧν ἐτρέφετο χρείας. Ἔπειθ᾿ ὅτι κἂν μέχρι σαρκὸς φθάνειν τὴν ἐκ τῆς τοιαύτης τροφῆς μεταβολὴν ὑποθοῖτό τις, οὐδ᾿ οὕτως ἀνάγκη τις ἔσται τὴν νεωστὶ μεταβληθεῖσαν ἐκ τῆς τοιᾶσδε τροφῆς σάρκα, προσπελάσασαν ἑτέρου τινὸς ἀνθρώπου σώματι, πάλιν ὡς μέρος εἰς τὴν ἐκείνου τελεῖν συμπλήρωσιν, τῷ μήτε αὐτὴν τὴν προσλαμβάνουσαν σάρκα πάντοτε φυλάττειν ἣν προσείληφε, μήτε τὴν ἑνωθεῖσαν ταύτῃ μόνιμον εἶναι καὶ παραμένειν ᾗ προσετέθη, πολλὴν δὲ καὶ τὴν ἐπὶ θάτερα δέχεσθαι μεταβολήν, ποτὲ μὲν πόνοις ἢ φροντίσι διαφορουμένην, ἄλλοτε δὲ λύπαις ἢ καμάτοις ἢ νόσοις συντηκομένην, καὶ ταῖς ἐξ ἐγκαύσεως ἢ περιψύξεως ἐπιγενομέναις δυσκρασίαις, μὴ συμμεταβαλλομένων σαρκὶ καὶ πιμελῇ τῶν δημῶν ἐν τῷ μένειν ἅπερ ἐστὶν τὴν τροφὴν δεχομένων. Τοιούτων δὲ γινομένων ἐπὶ τῆς σαρκὸς παθημάτων, πολύ γ᾿ ἔτι μᾶλλον εὕροι τις ἂν ταῦτα πάσχουσαν τὴν ἐξ ἀνοικείων τρεφομένην σάρκα, νῦν μὲν εἰς ὄγκον προϊοῦσαν καὶ πιαινομένην ἐξ ὦν προσείληφεν, εἶτα πάλιν ἀποπτύουσαν ὃν ἂν τύχῃ τρόπον καὶ μειουμένην ἢ μιᾷ τινι τῶν ἔμπροσθεν ῥηθεισῶν αἰτιῶν ἢ πλείοσι· μόνα δὲ παραμένειν τοῖς μέρεσιν ἃ συνδεῖν ἢ στέγειν ἢ θάλπειν πέφυκεν τὴν ὑπὸ τῆς φύσεως ἐξειλεγμένην καὶ τούτοις προσπεφυκυῖαν οἷς τὴν κατὰ φύσιν συνεξέπλησε ζωὴν καὶ τοὺς ἐν τῇ ζωῇ πόνους. Ἀλλ᾿ οὔτε γὰρ καθ᾿ ὃ δεῖ κρινομένων τῶν ἔναγχος ἐξητασμένων, οὔτε κατὰ συγχώρησιν παραδεχθέντων τῶν ἐπ᾿ ἐκείνοις γεγυμνασμένων, ἀληθὲς δεικνύναι δυνατὸν τὸ πρὸς αὐτῶν λεγόμενον, οὔτ᾿ ἂν συγκραθείη ποτὲ τὰ τῶν ἀνθρώπων σώματα τοῖς τῆς αὐτῆς οὖσι φύσεως, κἂν ὑπ᾿ ἀγνοίας ποτὲ κλαπῶσι τὴν αἴσθησιν δι᾿ ἑτέρου τινὸς μετασχόντες τοιούτου σώματος, κἂν αὐτόθεν ὑπ᾿ ἐνδείας ἢ μανίας ὁμοειδοῦς τινος μιανθῶσι σώματι· εἴ γε μὴ λελήθασιν ἡμᾶς ἀνθρωποειδεῖς τινες ὄντες θῆρες, ἢ μικτὴν ἔχοντες φύσιν ἐξ ἀνθρώπων καὶ θηρίων, οἵους πλάττειν εἰώθασιν οἱ τολμηρότεροι τῶν ποιητῶν.
pass_a_gloss: But even if someone should allow the nourishment entering from these things, and this is assumed more commonly, and even if it is contrary to nature, to be distinguished and changed into one of the moistening or drying or heating or cooling things, not even thus will anything useful come to be from the things allowed to them, of the bodies rising again from their own parts being reassembled, since none of the aforementioned parts exists, nor does it have the relation or order of a part, nor does it remain always to the parts of the body being nourished, or rise again with the rising bodies, nothing contributing any longer to living, neither blood nor phlegm nor bile nor spirit. For neither do the nourished bodies ever need, nor will they need, with the need of the nourished things having been taken away along with the decay of the need from which they were nourished. And since if someone should suppose the change from such nourishment to reach as far as flesh, not even thus will there be a necessity for the flesh newly changed from such nourishment, having come near to another human body, to complete again as a part, since neither the flesh taking it up keeps always what it took, nor is the flesh joined to it remaining and staying as it was added, but rather it undergoes much change, sometimes being differentiated by pains or cares, at other times being consumed by sorrows or toils or diseases, and by the bad mixtures coming from burning or chilling, the flesh and fat of the parts not changing along with the things being nourished. And with such passions happening to the flesh, one would find much more that the flesh nourished from openings suffers these things, now proceeding to a mass and being nourished from what it took, then again falling away in whatever way it happens and being lessened either by one of the aforementioned causes or by many. But only the parts remain which are suited by nature to bind or hold or nourish the life chosen by nature and the toils in life. But neither when judging the things recently examined as they should be, nor according to the concession of the things trained upon them, is it possible to show the truth of what is said against them, nor would the human bodies ever be preserved to have the same nature, even if they should seize the sensation through another such body due to ignorance, even if they should be defiled by a similar body due to need or madness; for if we have not forgotten, there are certain human-like beasts, or having a mixed nature from humans and beasts, which the bolder poets are accustomed to fashion.

choices.english: the nourishment entering from these things
rejected: the food coming from these things
the nourishment that comes from these things

pass_b_english: But even if someone concedes that nourishment entering from these sources—and this is the more common assumption—is somehow distinguished and transformed into something that moistens, dries, heats, or cools, despite being contrary to nature, still nothing useful will result for the reconstruction of bodies rising again from their own parts, since none of the aforementioned parts exists, nor does it hold the relation or order of a part, nor does it remain permanently attached to the nourished body or rise with the resurrected bodies, contributing nothing further to life—neither blood, nor phlegm, nor bile, nor spirit. For the bodies that once needed nourishment will not need it then either, because the very need of what was nourished is taken away along with the decay of the need from which they were sustained.

And even if someone supposes that the transformation from such nourishment reaches as far as flesh, it still does not follow that flesh newly formed from such nourishment, merely by coming near another human body, must again serve as a part completing that body's fullness; for the flesh that receives it does not always retain what it has taken, nor does the flesh joined to it remain fixed and permanent, but rather undergoes great change—sometimes altered by pains or anxieties, sometimes consumed by griefs, toils, or diseases, and by the imbalances arising from burning or chilling—while the flesh and fat of the limbs do not change along with the nourishment they receive. Given such passions in the flesh, one would find all the more that flesh nourished from foreign sources suffers these things: now swelling into a mass and being fed by what it absorbed, then again casting off whatever it happens to shed and diminishing, whether by one of the aforementioned causes or by many. Only those parts remain that nature has fitted to bind, shelter, or warm the life ordained by nature and the toils within that life.

Thus, neither by judging the inner elements as they ought to be judged, nor by accepting the concessions granted to the arguments built upon them, can the claim made against us be shown true; nor would human bodies ever be preserved with the same nature, even if they seized sensation through another such body in ignorance, or were defiled by a similar body through need or madness—unless we have forgotten that there exist human‑shaped beasts, or beings of mixed nature from humans and beasts, such as the bolder poets are accustomed to invent.

review.notes: The translation accurately captures the complex conditional and concessive structures of the Greek text. Pass A preserves the nuances of the Greek clauses, and Pass B provides a fluent rendering that remains faithful to the meaning and logical flow of the original. All technical terms (e.g., the four qualities, the bodily fluids, the concept of 'need' vs 'decay') are handled correctly.
